1003509.etyen:
Borrowed from English Swati (“the Swati language”), with English ⟨w⟩ adapted as Norwegian ⟨v⟩.
The English name is ultimately from either Swazi siSwati (“the Swati language”) or emaSwati (“the Swati people”), the singular of the latter being liSwati (“a Swati person”). These forms contain the noun-class prefixes si- (“class 7 prefix”), ema- (“class 6 prefix”) and li- (“class 5 prefix”), attached to the stem -Swati, which is based on the royal name Mswati. Doublet of swazi (“member of the Swati people”).
The spelling svati was officially standardized for both Bokmål and Nynorsk by Språkrådet on

en.g: goodbye, take care; a friendly farewell wishing the addressee well
x: Takk for besøket. Ha det fint!
Mannen ser på meg og sier «ha det fint, og pass deg for guttene».
The man looks at me and says “take care, and watch out for the boys”.

1005045.etyen:
A fixed phrase consisting of the imperative ha (“to have”), the pronoun det (“it”) and adverbial fint (“well, nicely”), the neuter singular of fin (“fine, nice”), literally “have it nice”. As a farewell, the phrase expresses a wish for the addressee's continued well-being.
The final part fin (“fine, nice”) is from late Old Norse fínn (“fine, polished”), ultimately from Latin finis (“end, limit”), with the semantic development through the sense “finished, perfected”.
Compare Norwegian Nynorsk ha det fint and Danish have det fint (“to be well, be doing well”).
